name: Expertise Ladder
causal_claim: In a frequent enthusiast ritual, stage-appropriate education and compatibility guidance can convert recurring workflow problems into a progression of trusted purchases without encouraging unnecessary upgrades.
why_it_might_work: Coffee is a frequent home ritual with an identifiable progression from beginner to enthusiast.
The result depends on interactions among skill, beans, water, workflow, maintenance, and equipment.
Education can make an offer more useful while explicitly identifying when an upgrade is unnecessary.

supporting_evidence.proposition: NCA reports that 66 percent of American adults drank coffee in the past day in Spring 2025.
supporting_evidence.interpretation_limit: Coffee participation does not establish demand for espresso education or gear.

supporting_evidence.proposition: A public NCA snapshot reports that most coffee drinkers prepared coffee at home and specialty consumption had grown since 2021.
supporting_evidence.interpretation_limit: The public snapshot is dated and the full method and segment economics are not available without the paid report.

contradicting_evidence.proposition: Credible recommendations may require machine-specific expertise and continuously updated compatibility knowledge.
contradicting_evidence.interpretation_limit: No support-time measurement or compatibility corpus has been collected.

contradicting_evidence.proposition: Customers may trust independent creators and communities more than a retailer that profits from the recommendation.
contradicting_evidence.interpretation_limit: No source-attribution study or customer interview has tested this concern.

required_conditions: A recurring workflow problem must appear across more than one machine or preparation context.
Customers must use education or compatibility information in actual purchase decisions.
The first solution space avoids electrical, pressure-bearing, and fragile equipment.
Content maintenance and support cost remain proportionate to contribution margin.
failure_conditions: Dominant problems are machine-specific and require expert troubleshooting.
Customers consume education but purchase solely from the lowest-price marketplace listing.
Progression depends on promoting unnecessary upgrades that conflict with ACE's trust standard.
Compatibility churn makes guidance obsolete before it earns back its maintenance cost.

falsification_experiment.question: Does education resolve a recurring cross-context coffee workflow problem that affects actual buying behavior?
falsification_experiment.hypothesis: At least one workflow or compatibility problem recurs across authorized reviews and customers' past purchases, and education materially influenced how they chose a solution.
falsification_experiment.null_hypothesis: Problems are machine-specific, aesthetic, or content-only and do not create a scalable commercial mechanism.
evidence_sources: At least 100 authorized or user-provided reviews across beginner workflow, maintenance, and compatibility contexts and at least two sources.
Five structured interviews spanning beginner and experienced home coffee preparation.
sampling_plan: Remove duplicates and preserve source, product context, machine context, rating, and date.
Predeclare mess, cleaning, wasted inputs, compatibility, consistency, and upgrade-regret themes.
Ask customers to reconstruct their last purchase and information path before asking opinions about education.
survival_criteria: At least one actionable theme appears in 15 or more nonduplicate reviews, across all three contexts and both sources.
At least three of five interviewees identify information or compatibility evidence that changed an actual purchase or prevented one.
The problem admits a cross-platform first test without electrical or pressure-bearing products.
falsification_criteria: No problem transfers across contexts and sources.
Purchase histories show that education is consumed but does not affect selection behavior.
A credible recommendation requires machine-specific support that defeats lean automation.
known_confounders: Enthusiast communities may overrepresent high-spending and technically confident users.
Review complaints can reflect poor technique rather than product failure.
Interviewees may rationalize purchases after the fact.
prohibited_actions: No scraping, advertising, inventory, affiliate publishing, supplier outreach, or equipment purchase.
falsification_experiment.next_decision: Reject the mechanism or advance one cross-platform workflow problem to a no-inventory information-choice test.

confidence_rationale: Participation and ritual frequency are observed; the link between education, purchase behavior, and scalable economics is not.

boundary_conditions: The first instance is limited to home coffee workflow and excludes machines, electrical parts, and pressure-bearing components.
transferability.next_replication_test: After one instance passes, test the education-and-progression mechanism in a second enthusiast hobby with independent evidence.
